summary: Maya Chen's repository matches the resume. Pulseboard has a long commit history, a passing build, and tests around the websocket path the role needs.
consensus: The websocket fanout, the ingest pipeline, and the socket tests are in the repository.
The dates on the resume line up with a multi-year commit history.
questionsForHR: Ask which part of the ingest pipeline she would redesign on a higher volume.
Ask how the on-call rotation used the board during an incident.
Ask what she left untested on purpose.
Ask how she would split ownership of the client and the pipeline on this team.
Ask for the production incident she is least proud of and what changed afterward.

reviews.headline: The scope she claims is the scope the commit history supports.

strengths.text: She owned the board from ingest through the UI across several years.
strengths.evidence: Resume: Pulseboard (Feb 2023 – Oct 2026). First commit 2023-02-11, last commit 2026-10-18, 146 active days.

drawbacks.text: The resume does not say what she explicitly left out of scope.
drawbacks.evidence: The project description lists the protocol, the pipeline, and the React UI, and stops there.

reviews.headline: The architecture in the resume is the architecture in the source, and the build passes.

strengths.text: Socket fanout, retries, and end-to-end protocol tests are all present.
strengths.evidence: src/server/hub.ts, src/pipeline/ingest.ts, and tests/socket.e2e.ts. Build log: tsc and vite build succeeded. 42 tests passed.

drawbacks.text: A single largest commit still holds 11% of the lines, which is healthy but worth a glance.

reviews.headline: I would hand her a pipeline ticket in the first week.

strengths.text: The code is organized around the same words she uses in the resume.
strengths.evidence: TypeScript, TSX, and SQL are split across hub, ingest, and tests rather than one generated file.

drawbacks.text: I cannot tell from the repo alone how she reviews other people's code.
drawbacks.evidence: 391 of 428 commits are hers, so most of the history is solo.

crossExam.text: Agreed on the dates. I was looking for a gap between the README and the tests, and I did not find one.
The socket tests are readable. A new teammate could extend them without a guided tour.
